This same thing happened with Ron Paul. The unfortunate reality is that bringing a new platform around requires us to maintain reasonable goals. Saying "I like him, but he can't win" is the kind of thing that can then be transitioned into "but if we work hard for 8 or 16 years, then we'll have a chance at real change!" When a candidate who truly can't win (and Sanders truly can't, the established system simply will not let him right now) starts to drum up "really could win" rhetoric, then you not only fail to lay the groundwork for the future, but also risk alienating a huge percentage of your base when you inevitably lose.

Simply put: if you think voting for Sanders makes you progressive and think "he really can win," you're just the most recent generation being taken along the circle-jerk, and will likely be disillusioned to politics for life beyond this election. If, however, you've joined the Socialist Party and are talking about the people coming up in 2020 or 2024, then yes, those people legitimately really can win, and you really are the kind of person to make it happen.
